column1: # Probe matrix for scripts/gradient_routing/run_corpus_loss_probes.sh.
# Each row is one eval-only probe: score CHECKPOINT on CORPUS using
# configs/gradient_routing/nemotron_nano_corpus_loss_probe.yaml. Rows run serially.
# The three arms are matched: control and gr_off both start from base, both consume
# 503,316,480 tokens of EACH corpus over 120 iterations at GBS 1024 x seq 8192, and
# both are scored here on identical batches. They differ only in how the two corpora
# are presented (blended 50/50 batches vs label-homogeneous iterations) and in whether
# gradient routing is applied.
#   base     stock Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-Base-BF16 — the pre-CPT anchor. Learning is
#            measured as the drop from this, so a raw loss without it is uninterpretable.
#   control  blended no-GR CPT on both corpora (configs/.../nemotron_nano_control_blended_cpt.yaml)
#   gr_off   the gradient-routing run, loaded WITHOUT its gr_aux keys — the forget_off
#            export posture. See the probe config's header for why that load is exact.
#   filtering  retain corpus only, 60 iters, never saw the forget data. The ceiling that
#            routing is trying to approximate, and the paper's actual comparison point.
#            Matched on retain tokens (503,316,480) but not on optimizer steps. It is an
#            OVERRIDE of the control config, not a config of its own — the exact launch
#            line is in that config's header.
# CHECKPOINT paths below duplicate `checkpoint.save` in the configs that produce them.
# Change a config's save directory and the matching row here goes stale, so change both.
# Scoring each arm on BOTH corpora is deliberate: retain answers "does routing cost
# retained learning" (the question), forget answers "did routing keep the forget content
# out of core" (the point of the method). One without the other is not a result.
# Columns (tab-separated): NAME  CHECKPOINT  DATA_PREFIX
NAME
base_retain
base_forget
control_retain
control_forget
gr_off_retain
gr_off_forget
filtering_retain
